seoTitle: Export Smartsheet to Excel Without Losing Data
metaDescription: Download your Smartsheet project as a formatted Excel file using the native Export utility, and see how column types and hierarchies translate.
intro: Sharing data with offline stakeholders or building a local pivot table means getting your Smartsheet data into Excel cleanly. This guide covers using the native export tool, understanding how column types like dropdowns and dates convert, and what happens to hierarchies and comments in the process.

steps.heading: Open the file menu
steps.body: Go to the top-left menu on your sheet dashboard to find the Export utility panel.

steps.heading: Select Export to Microsoft Excel
steps.body: Run the native export function to compile your sheet rows into a .xlsx file.

steps.heading: Understand column type conversion
steps.body: Know what happens to Dropdowns, Contact Lists, and Dates during the conversion into standard Excel columns.

steps.heading: Check hierarchy and grouping
steps.body: Review how indented parent-child task hierarchies and row grouping translate into the Excel file.

steps.heading: Export additional elements
steps.body: Include row comments, discussions, and attached documentation as needed when exporting.

faq.question: Will my dropdown columns still work after exporting to Excel?
faq.answer: Dropdown, Contact List, and Date columns convert into standard Excel formats, so the interactive functionality doesn't carry over as-is.

faq.question: Do parent-child hierarchies survive the export?
faq.answer: Indented task hierarchies and row grouping generally translate, though it's worth reviewing the file after export to confirm.

faq.question: Can I export row comments along with the data?
faq.answer: Yes, you can include individual row comments, discussions, and attached documentation in the export.

faq.question: Will formulas transfer over correctly?
faq.answer: Formula translations can shift during export, so it's a good idea to double-check calculated values after opening the file in Excel.
